conflicts: 235U ground-level hyperfine constants: Avril et al. 1994 (as tabulated by Savukov 2020) give A = -60.54 MHz, B = 4074 MHz; the Childs et al. atomic-beam values quoted by Wei et al. 2021 are |A| = 2.0186(1) mK = 60.516 MHz (printed without sign) and B = 136.805(7) mK = 4101.3 MHz. The B values differ by 27 MHz; the sign of A was taken from the Avril/Savukov table. Neither original was opened.

Lifetime of the 16900.386 cm^-1 level (5f3.6d.7s.7p 7M7): 205(20) ns (Klose & Voigt 1977), 255(25) ns (Carlson et al. 1976), 232(25) ns (Carlson et al. 1977), all second-hand from Savukov 2020, who adopts 231(25) ns.

235U hyperfine constants of the 14643.867 cm^-1 level: Harilal et al. 2020 fit A = 20.1(3) MHz, B = 4950(120) MHz and state that this differs significantly from earlier literature values (not opened).

Transition probabilities: the Corliss (1976) arc values are stated by their author to differ systematically from Voigt's (1975) oscillator strengths (smaller below 424 nm, larger above); for 0 - 15631.855 cm^-1 the laser measurement of Hackel & Rushford is the entry and the Corliss value, where present, is kept as an alternative.

Configuration of the 11613.975 cm^-1 level: 5f3.7s2.7p 5K5 in the Laboratoire Aime Cotton table; Wei et al. 2021 note that 5f2.6d2.7s2 has also been proposed and that their hyperfine constants favour 5f3.7s2.7p.

Selected-wavelength table versus level tables: the archived wavelength table has several misprints in the truncated level energies (e.g. '19 985' for 19885.515, '29 904' for 29909.539, '10 288' for 10208.488) and four wavelengths with a corrupted decimal point; the level pair was always fixed by J and the observed wavenumber, and each affected line says so in its note.
not_found: 404.249 nm line from the 620 cm^-1 level used as second colour in the uranium RIMS scheme of Savina & Trappitsch: no even level of the Laboratoire Aime Cotton tables reproduces this wavelength from 620.323 cm^-1 within 0.6 cm^-1, so the line is not entered
the autoionizing / high-lying levels of the multistep photoionization schemes (above 30000 cm^-1) are not entered

oscillator strengths of Bieniewski (J. Opt. Soc. Am. B 1, 300 (1984); OSTI 6125793, no full text), Voigt (1975), Henrion et al. (J. Quant. Spectrosc. Radiat. Transfer 37, 477 (1987)), Kapoor et al. (358.48 nm line) and recent laser-induced-breakdown work: not opened

lifetimes quoted by Corliss from Janes et al. for the levels '23433' (155 ns) and '23212' (170 ns): no level at 23433 cm^-1 and two levels at 23212 cm^-1 (J=2 and J=5) in the level tables, so they could not be assigned and are not entered
Corliss' own 'lifetimes' (Table 2) are upper limits computed from summed transition probabilities and are deliberately not stored

the Los Alamos atlas itself (Palmer, Keller, Engleman, LA-8251-MS, https://www.osti.gov/servlets/purl/5095995) was downloaded, but its tables are only available as poor OCR text; intensities were therefore taken from the Laboratoire Aime Cotton selected-wavelength table, which is based on it
Kurucz line lists: no uranium file exists at kurucz.harvard.edu/atoms/9200 (directory empty except a date file)

lines at 394.83 nm (Phillips et al., as cited by Wei et al. 2021) and 401.91 nm (Los Alamos atomic-beam work): not identified with a level pair, not entered; the 404.28 nm line cited with them is presumably 620.323 - 25348.977 cm^-1 (404.275 nm air), which is in the file without a use annotation
notes: Levels and classifications: archived online version (2017 captures of the level tables, 2002 capture of the wavelength table) of the Blaise & Wyart actinide tables (Laboratoire Aime Cotton); energies are for 238U and stated to be accurate to about 0.003 cm^-1. NIST ASD lists only the ground level and the limit 49958.4(5) cm^-1 (no newer measurement found, so no ionization_limit entry). Configurations are stored without parent terms (full printed string in each level note); terms printed in parentheses (leading component 25-50 %) are stored without parentheses. 'relative_intensity' is the hollow-cathode emission intensity printed in the selected-wavelength table (atlas scale) and only ranks lines. A_s values from Corliss 1976 are arc-intensity values of low accuracy (see each note); they were read from the scanned PDF by text extraction and accepted only if the printed gA, gf and log gf were mutually consistent and the wavelength matched a unique level pair. Isotope shifts are nu(235U) - nu(238U), derived from the tabulated level shifts (the 235U line lies at higher wavenumber when the value is positive). The selection is: the lines with a laser-spectroscopy use, the 48 strongest tabulated lines from the ground level and the 620 cm^-1 level, and the strongest lines from higher levels, all with upper level below about 30000 cm^-1.
